# Archiving object graphs

An archive is an ordinary R list that stores the state of robjc objects and the relationships between their references.
`RSKeyedArchiver` creates this list, and `RSKeyedUnarchiver` restores it.
Use R's `saveRDS()` and `readRDS()` to write it to a file and read it back.
We start with a built-in class, then move to shared references and a graph containing custom classes.

## Archive and restore built-in classes

`RSKeyedArchiver$new()$encode(root)` creates an archive from the supplied root value.
To restore it, pass the archive to `RSKeyedUnarchiver$new()` and call `decode()`.
Built-in robjc classes resolve automatically, so they need no manual class mapping.

```{r}
library(robjc)

original <- RSString$new("saved text")
archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$encode(original)
stopifnot(is.list(archive))

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(archive, path)
saved <- readRDS(path)
unlink(path)

decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(saved)
restored <- decoder$decode()
stopifnot(restored$isMemberOf(RSString))
stopifnot(identical(restored$value(), "saved text"))
```

The archive includes information about the saved class, but `decode()` uses its currently loaded class generator.
It does not take the original RObjC instance directly from the RDS file.

## Preserve shared references

The archive records when multiple locations refer to the same instance.
Both elements of the following list point to `shared`. After restoration, they point to the same new instance.

```{r}
shared <- RSString$new("shared")
shared_archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$encode(list(shared, shared))
shared_decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(shared_archive)
loaded <- shared_decoder$decode()

stopifnot(identical(loaded[[1L]], loaded[[2L]]))
stopifnot(!identical(loaded[[1L]], shared))
stopifnot(identical(loaded[[1L]]$value(), "shared"))
```

`isEqual()` could check whether the values match. Here, `identical()` verifies that the **reference remains shared**.
robjc objects inside ordinary lists are also processed recursively.

## Archive several root objects together

`archive()` accepts one argument.
To save several independent objects in one archive, put them in a named R `list` and pass that list as the root value.
Decoding returns a list with the same names.

```{r}
first <- RSString$new("first")
second <- RSNumber$new(2L)
roots <- list(first = first, second = second, first_again = first)

roots_archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$encode(roots)
restored_roots <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(roots_archive)$decode()

stopifnot(identical(names(restored_roots), names(roots)))
stopifnot(identical(restored_roots$first$value(), "first"))
stopifnot(identical(restored_roots$second$value(), 2L))
stopifnot(identical(restored_roots$first, restored_roots$first_again))
stopifnot(!identical(restored_roots$first, first))
```

`first` and `second` are restored as separate objects.
Because `first_again` refers to the same source object as `first`, both entries refer to the same restored instance.

## Inspect archived classes before decoding

`RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(archive)` loads the data but does not yet restore instances.
Follow its prompt to inspect or adjust class mappings, if needed, before calling `decode()`.
`classMappings()` returns a tibble of classes that need attention. By default, it omits classes that resolved automatically.

```{r}
stopifnot(nrow(decoder$classMappings()) == 0L)
all_classes <- decoder$classMappings(include_automatic = TRUE)
stopifnot(identical(all_classes$class_name, "RSString"))
stopifnot(identical(all_classes$status, "automatic"))
stopifnot(identical(all_classes$decoder_class[[1L]], RSString))
stopifnot(identical(decoder$classMappingForKey(all_classes$class_key[[1L]])$status, "automatic"))
```

For this example, selected columns of `classMappings(include_automatic = TRUE)` look like this.
The default `classMappings()` view is a zero-row tibble because it omits this automatically resolved row.

| `class_key` | `class_name` | `version` | `decoder_name` | `status` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| C1 | RSString | 0.2.0 | RSString | automatic |

The actual tibble also includes `package`, `class_id`, `kind`, and `decoder_class`, which are omitted here.
`decoder_name` is for display; `decoder_class` holds the generator used to restore the object.

`class_name` and `version` describe the saved class. `decoder_class` is a list column of destination generators.
`class_key` identifies a class mapping within this archive when you edit it.
Use `include_automatic = TRUE` to display all classes.
`classMappingsAsDictionary()` always returns every class as an `RSMutableDictionary`. Its keys are `RSString` objects wrapping `class_key` values, and its values are destination generators.

```{r}
class_dictionary <- decoder$classMappingsAsDictionary()
stopifnot(class_dictionary$isKindOf(RSMutableDictionary))
stopifnot(identical(
  class_dictionary$objectForKey(RSString$new(all_classes$class_key[[1L]])),
  RSString
))
```

## Map custom classes

A class defined only in a script cannot resolve through package registration.
For such a class, put its current generator in the `classMappings()` result and pass the edited table to `setClassMappings()`.
The saved class name and destination class name need not match.
The destination's `initWithCoder()` must, however, understand the saved fields.
**`setClassMappings()` selects a destination class; it does not transform the fields.**
Implement migration between versions or classes in the destination's `initWithCoder()`.
The next example moves an old `text` field to a new `title` field.
During restoration, `savedClassVersion()` returns the saved class version.

```{r}
LegacyNote <- RSObjectClass(
  "Guide10LegacyNote", version = "1.0",
  protocols = list(RSCoding),
  public = list(
    text = NULL,
    initialize = function(text) {
      super$initialize()
      self$text <- text
      invisible(self)
    },
    encodeWithCoder = function(coder) {
      coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$text, "text")
      invisible(self)
    },
    initWithCoder = function(coder) {
      self$text <- coder$decodeObjectForKey("text")
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

CurrentNote <- RSObjectClass(
  "Guide10CurrentNote", version = "2.0",
  protocols = list(RSCoding),
  public = list(
    title = NULL,
    initialize = function(title) {
      super$initialize()
      self$title <- title
      invisible(self)
    },
    encodeWithCoder = function(coder) {
      coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$title, "title")
      invisible(self)
    },
    initWithCoder = function(coder) {
      saved_key <- if (identical(coder$savedClassVersion(), "1.0")) "text" else "title"
      self$title <- coder$decodeObjectForKey(saved_key)
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)
```

The old archive appears as unresolved. Set its `decoder_class` to `CurrentNote` before restoring it.
`setClassMappings()` accepts a tibble with `class_key` and `decoder_class` columns.
Use `classMappingForKey()` to inspect one mapping.

```{r}
legacy_archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$encode(LegacyNote$new("draft"))
custom_decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(legacy_archive)
classes <- custom_decoder$classMappings()
stopifnot(identical(classes$class_name, "Guide10LegacyNote"))
stopifnot(identical(classes$status, "unresolved"))

classes$decoder_class[1L] <- list(CurrentNote)
custom_decoder$setClassMappings(classes)
stopifnot(identical(custom_decoder$classMappingForKey(classes$class_key[[1L]])$status, "manual"))

current <- custom_decoder$decode()
stopifnot(current$isMemberOf(CurrentNote))
stopifnot(identical(current$title, "draft"))
```

Before mapping, selected columns of `custom_decoder$classMappings()` contain this row.
`NA` in `decoder_name` means that no destination has been selected.

| `class_key` | `class_name` | `version` | `decoder_name` | `status` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| C1 | Guide10LegacyNote | 1.0 | NA | unresolved |

After `setClassMappings(classes)`, `decoder_name` becomes `Guide10CurrentNote` and `status` becomes `manual`.
`class_name` and `version` retain their saved values.

You can also supply an `RSMutableDictionary` mapping.
An unresolved class has `RSNull$null` as its value. The returned dictionary is an independent mapping snapshot, so call `setClassMappings()` after editing it.

```{r}
other_decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(legacy_archive)
mapping <- other_decoder$classMappingsAsDictionary()
key <- RSString$new(classes$class_key[[1L]])
stopifnot(identical(mapping$objectForKey(key), RSNull$null))

mapping$setObjectForKey(CurrentNote, key)
other_decoder$setClassMappings(mapping)
stopifnot(identical(other_decoder$decode()$title, "draft"))
```

## Implement class coding methods

To archive a custom class, assign keys to fields in `encodeWithCoder(coder)` and read them back in `initWithCoder(coder)`.
Declaring adoption of `RSCoding` checks that both methods exist when the class is created.
The archiver records references so that the same object is not encoded twice.

The decoder uses `robjc_allocate()` to create a destination instance without calling its normal `initialize()`, then passes it to `initWithCoder()`.
The arguments needed for ordinary construction may no longer be available, and the fields may have changed since the archive was saved.
Implement migration in `initWithCoder()`, as shown above.

An extension package can register a class with `robjc_register_class()` in its `.onLoad()` function.
Registered classes generally need no manual `setClassMappings()` call. Keep the registration `id` stable independently of the class name and version.
See `?robjc_register_class` for the registration arguments and procedure.

## Handle unresolved classes and invalid archives

Calling `decode()` with an unresolved class raises an error listing its unresolved `class_key`.
Inspect the row with `classMappings()` and assign an appropriate generator.
An archive with an unsupported format fails when the Unarchiver is created; a broken reference or field can fail during restoration.

```{r}
unresolved_decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(legacy_archive)
unresolved_error <- tryCatch(unresolved_decoder$decode(), error = identity)
stopifnot(inherits(unresolved_error, "error"))
stopifnot(grepl("Unresolved archive classes", conditionMessage(unresolved_error), fixed = TRUE))

invalid_archive <- legacy_archive
invalid_archive$format <- "unknown-format"
invalid_error <- tryCatch(RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(invalid_archive), error = identity)
stopifnot(inherits(invalid_error, "error"))
```

For a round-trip test, verify shared references as well as values and classes.
When implementing migration, test the destination state using an archive from an older version.
For a graph with several custom classes, see the [Practical Encoding Appendix](appendix_practical_encoding.Rmd).
